chunks: From him, from his father, from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Hammad, from Isḥaq ibn 'Ammar and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He asked me, 'Does the judgment of Ibn Abi Layla differ among you?' I said, 'Yes. In one case, he gave four different rulings regarding a woman whose husband dies, and their respective families dispute the household goods (mata' al-bayt). He ruled in it according to the opinion of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i: Whatever is the household goods of the man, it belongs to the man, and he mentioned the same as equal, except that he said,
Except for the scale, for it is from the household goods of the man.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on household goods division according to Ibn Abi Layla and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the method of *taqlid* (following a jurist) in early Shia jurisprudence by examining the divergent rulings of the prominent Iraqi jurist Ibn Abi Layla regarding the division of household goods (*mata' al-bayt*) after a husband's death. It specifically highlights his adherence to the Hanafi-leaning opinion of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, which distinguishes between general household items and specific tools like the weighing scale, thereby clarifying the scope of marital property division. This narration serves as a key example of how early Imams validated and critiqued the legal reasoning of contemporary jurists to guide the Shia community in practical matters of inheritance and property.
